obligations.note: The change edits Underwriting.decide, which is in CRD-1 scope. The approve/refer/decline logic and the 40/90 thresholds look unchanged, and the exhaustive-labelled grid control test autoApproveGridMatchesPolicy passed. But the proof over all DTI/LTV values (ACR-0406) has lapsed, and the grid (DTI in 0.01 steps, LTV in whole numbers 50-110) does not establish the property over the full domain.

Ledger evidence ACR-0406 (non-rerunnable Rocq proof on d30b2ad) covers Underwriting.decide. This change alters its return value (reasons go from [] to ["POLICY_SATISFIED"]), which is a behaviour change, so the evidence lapses. No new evidence of the same strength was supplied, yet the change request relies on the existing ledger entry.

Ticket CHG-26899 is a standard ticket, approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) at 2026-10-10T00:50Z before review. Its component mortgage.underwriting covers the only touched path, Underwriting.java.
The code_review approval is from wen.li@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and a different person from the author Priya Raman.
The approval names head commit 1507ccd, which is the only commit in the change.

run.json records success on head 1507ccd. The JUnit report shows 124 tests with 0 failures and 0 skipped, including controls.UnderwritingControlTest#autoApproveGridMatchesPolicy. I could not rerun locally because the JUnit jar is missing, and the report timestamps/hostname do not match run.json.
The only touched component, mortgage.underwriting, is not security_sensitive, so no security review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The change is not an emergency and the ticket type is standard, so no PIR is due.

summary: The change makes Underwriting.decide return a POLICY_SATISFIED reason for auto-approve-eligible decisions. That changes the behaviour of code covered by the non-rerunnable CRD-1 proof in the acceptance ledger (ACR-0406). Under LAP-1 that evidence lapses, and the change offers no replacement of the same strength; it relies on the lapsed ledger entry. Ticket, independent approval, approval coverage and CI on the final commit are all in order. The missing evidence still fails LAP-1 and leaves CRD-1 unestablished, so the change is rejected.
